title: Sponsor list performance with maximum sponsor data volume
scenario_description: Test sponsor list loading with a simulated dataset of 500 active sponsors and multiple pages, under moderate user load.
expected_outcome: Paginated sponsor lists render within 2 seconds for 95% of requests.

title: Sponsor list rendering and functionality across desktop browsers
scenario_description: Verify the sponsor list, including sorting, filtering, and pagination, renders and functions correctly on Chrome, Firefox, Safari, and Edge (latest stable versions).
expected_outcome: No layout issues, broken functionality, or unresponsive elements are observed on desktop browsers.

title: Sponsor list rendering and functionality on mobile devices
scenario_description: Verify the sponsor list displays and works correctly on mobile equivalents (iOS Safari, Android Chrome).
expected_outcome: The sponsor list content is responsive, readable, and fully functional on specified mobile browsers.

title: Cancellation terms acceptance on successful trainee registration
scenario_description: A trainee successfully registers, explicitly accepting the cancellation terms during the process.
expected_outcome: The 'cancellation_terms_accepted' flag is accurately set to true and permanently associated with the trainee's account.

title: Immutability of accepted cancellation terms after registration
scenario_description: After a trainee successfully accepts cancellation terms, attempt to modify the recorded status through standard application flows.
expected_outcome: The 'cancellation_terms_accepted' status remains true and cannot be altered by the user or regular system operations.

title: Unauthorized API attempt to modify accepted cancellation terms
scenario_description: Attempt to change a trainee's 'cancellation_terms_accepted' status directly via an unauthenticated or unauthorized API call.
expected_outcome: The modification attempt is rejected, and the system logs the unauthorized access attempt.

title: Direct database attempt to alter accepted cancellation terms
scenario_description: Attempt to modify or delete the 'cancellation_terms_accepted' flag for a trainee directly in the database using non-privileged access.
expected_outcome: The modification or deletion attempt is blocked by database constraints or permissions, or detected and logged as unauthorized.

title: Event addition reliability under concurrent user activity
scenario_description: Simulate 100 trainee users simultaneously adding events to their schedules.
expected_outcome: All events are successfully added to each trainee's schedule, immediately visible, and no data loss or conflicts occur.

title: Single event addition persistence and display speed
scenario_description: A single trainee adds an event to their schedule and immediately navigates to "my schedule".
expected_outcome: The event is successfully persisted and displayed in "my schedule" within 0.5 seconds.

title: Availability of "Add to My Schedule" over extended period
scenario_description: Continuously monitor the "Add to My Schedule" feature for functionality and accessibility over a 30-day period.
expected_outcome: The "Add to My Schedule" feature maintains at least 99.9% uptime throughout the monitoring period.

title: "Add to My Schedule" availability under peak load conditions
scenario_description: Monitor the availability of the "Add to My Schedule" feature during simulated peak event registration traffic.
expected_outcome: The feature remains available and functional, sustaining 99.9% uptime even during periods of high concurrency.

title: Venue details page load time for anonymous users
scenario_description: An anonymous user accesses the venue details page under typical system load conditions.
expected_outcome: The venue details page is fully loaded and interactive within 3 seconds for 90% of requests.

title: Venue page performance with heavy images and embedded map
scenario_description: Test the venue details page when it contains a high number of images and a complex embedded map, under normal user load.
expected_outcome: Despite rich content, the page remains interactive within 3 seconds for 90% of anonymous user requests.

title: Automated accessibility scan of venue details page
scenario_description: Conduct an automated accessibility audit on the venue details page using tools like axe-core.
expected_outcome: No critical or severe WCAG 2.1 Level AA violations are detected by automated tools.

title: Manual review of venue details content for WCAG compliance
scenario_description: Perform a manual accessibility review of the venue details page, focusing on keyboard navigation, semantic structure, and logical focus order.
expected_outcome: The venue details content meets all applicable WCAG 2.1 Level AA guidelines, with all interactive elements navigable and perceivable.

title: Comprehensive PCI DSS compliance audit for payment system
scenario_description: A certified QSA conducts a full PCI DSS v3.2.1 compliance audit of the payment processing system.
expected_outcome: The system passes the PCI DSS audit, with no critical non-conformities identified regarding payment card handling.

title: Verification of payment data encryption in transit and at rest
scenario_description: Inspect network traffic during payment submission and analyze the storage of payment-related data in the database.
expected_outcome: Payment card information is encrypted using TLS 1.2+ during transit and AES-256 at rest (if stored).

title: Definitive outcome for valid and invalid payment attempts
scenario_description: Process a mix of valid payment attempts and deliberately invalid ones (e.g., incorrect CVC, expired card, insufficient funds).
expected_outcome: Every valid attempt reaches a confirmed success, and every invalid attempt reaches a clear, documented failure state without ambiguity.

title: Payment system behavior during network interruptions
scenario_description: Simulate network connectivity issues or gateway timeouts during various stages of the payment transaction.
expected_outcome: The system consistently resolves to either a successful charge or a definite failure with no partial charges or phantom transactions.

title: Payment completion time under typical transaction volume
scenario_description: Process a batch of successful payment transactions under average system load and monitor completion times.
expected_outcome: 98% of successful payment transactions, from submission to confirmation, complete within 5 seconds.

title: Payment completion time under high concurrent transactions
scenario_description: Simulate a peak period of high concurrent payment submissions by multiple users.
expected_outcome: Even under peak load, 98% of successful transactions achieve completion within 5 seconds.

title: User-friendly error messages for standard payment failures
scenario_description: Initiate payment attempts using scenarios such as an expired card, incorrect CVC, and intentionally insufficient funds.
expected_outcome: The system displays clear, specific, and actionable error messages (e.g., "Card expired," "CVC incorrect") for each failure type.

title: Specific error messages for less common payment failures
scenario_description: Initiate payment attempts simulating less common issues, such as card issuer specific declines or general processing errors.
expected_outcome: The system provides informative error messages that help the user understand the issue, even if more generic (e.g., "Transaction declined by bank").

title: Anonymous user attempts sponsor link creation/modification
scenario_description: An unauthenticated (anonymous) user attempts to access or perform any sponsor linking actions (create, modify, delete).
expected_outcome: All attempts are denied with an "Access Denied" error or equivalent, and no unauthorized action is performed.

title: Non-sponsor authenticated user attempts sponsor link actions
scenario_description: An authenticated user with 'trainee' or general 'authenticateduser' role attempts to create, modify, or delete sponsor links.
expected_outcome: All attempts are denied with an "Access Denied" error, preventing any unauthorized sponsor linking actions.

title: Immediate persistence of newly created sponsor links and data
scenario_description: A sponsor creates new links and associates attendees with those links.
expected_outcome: All created links and associated attendance data are immediately and accurately reflected on the sponsorship page.

title: Sponsor link and attendance data accessibility post-event
scenario_description: Verify the availability and accuracy of sponsor links and associated attendance data at 30-day intervals for 6 months after the event concludes.
expected_outcome: All sponsor link and attendance data remains 100% accurate and accessible for the entire post-event viewing period.

title: Tagging system code adherence to Drupal standards
scenario_description: Conduct a code review of the tagging system implementation by an experienced Drupal developer.
expected_outcome: The tagging system utilizes standard Drupal APIs/components and adheres to Drupal coding best practices, requiring no custom, difficult-to-maintain code.

title: Ease of adding new tag terms to existing vocabulary
scenario_description: A Drupal developer attempts to add a new term to an existing tag vocabulary within the system.
expected_outcome: The developer successfully adds the new tag term and verifies its functionality in under 15 minutes.

title: Tag reflection for a single blog post after publication
scenario_description: An administrator publishes a new blog post with relevant tags.
expected_outcome: The tags are correctly associated with the post and appear in the relevant RSS feed or API endpoint for Drupal Planet within 1 minute.

title: Tag reflection for multiple blog posts published concurrently
scenario_description: An administrator publishes 10 blog posts with distinct tags in quick succession.
expected_outcome: All tags for all 10 posts are correctly associated and reflected in the Drupal Planet RSS feed or API within 1 minute of their respective publications.

title: Event list load time for user with many registered events
scenario_description: Simulate a user logged in with 20+ assigned events accessing their "my summits" page under anticipated peak load.
expected_outcome: The user's event list loads and displays within 1.5 seconds for 95% of requests.

title: Event list load time for typical number of registered events
scenario_description: Simulate a user logged in with an average number of registered events (e.g., 5-10) accessing their "my summits" page under normal load.
expected_outcome: The user's event list loads and displays well within 1.5 seconds for 95% of requests.

title: Immediate reflection of new event registrations in user list
scenario_description: An attendee successfully registers for a new event.
expected_outcome: The newly registered event immediately appears correctly in the attendee's "my summits" list.

title: Immediate reflection of event cancellations in user list
scenario_description: An attendee successfully cancels their registration for an event.
expected_outcome: The cancelled event is immediately removed or correctly marked as cancelled in the attendee's "my summits" list.

title: Anonymous user attempts to post a new job listing
scenario_description: An unauthenticated (anonymous) user attempts to access the "Post Job" functionality or submit a new job listing.
expected_outcome: The anonymous user is denied access to the feature and cannot submit a job listing.

title: Non-sponsor authenticated user attempts to post a job
scenario_description: An authenticated user with a 'trainee' or general 'authenticateduser' role attempts to post a new job listing.
expected_outcome: The non-'sponsor' authenticated user is denied access to the "Post Job" functionality and cannot submit a job listing.

title: Immediate storage and public visibility of new job listings
scenario_description: A sponsor successfully posts a new job listing, marked as publicly visible.
expected_outcome: The job listing is immediately stored, correctly associated with the sponsor, and visible on the public job board.

title: Job listing persistence over its specified duration
scenario_description: Verify the presence and integrity of job listings periodically (e.g., daily) throughout their specified public duration.
expected_outcome: All job listings remain accurately stored and publicly visible (if applicable) for their entire active period without loss or corruption.

title: Non-administrator user attempts to accept a session
scenario_description: An authenticated user (e.g., trainee, sponsor, or general authenticated user) attempts to change a session's status to 'accepted'.
expected_outcome: The system denies the attempt with an "Access Denied" error or equivalent, preventing unauthorized session status changes.

title: Anonymous user attempts to accept a session
scenario_description: An unauthenticated (anonymous) user attempts to change a session's status to 'accepted' (e.g., via a direct API call).
expected_outcome: The system denies the attempt, typically requiring authentication first, and prevents any unauthorized action.

title: Single session acceptance and immediate status reflection
scenario_description: An administrator marks a single session as 'accepted' through the administrative interface.
expected_outcome: The session's status is reliably updated to 'accepted', immediately reflected in all relevant UI views and API endpoints.

title: Multiple session acceptances and status persistence after restart
scenario_description: An administrator accepts 10 sessions. Immediately after, simulate a system restart or database failover.
expected_outcome: All 10 sessions retain their 'accepted' status after system recovery, and the status is accurately reflected across all views.

title: Verification of speaker registration data encryption in transit
scenario_description: A speaker submits their registration form. Network traffic is intercepted and analyzed during the submission.
expected_outcome: All speaker registration data is transmitted encrypted using TLS 1.2 or a stronger protocol.

title: Verification of speaker registration data encryption at rest
scenario_description: After a speaker successfully registers, attempt to access the stored registration data directly from the database.
expected_outcome: Speaker registration data, including personal and session details, is stored in the database using AES-256 encryption.

title: Speaker registration reliability under 50 concurrent submissions
scenario_description: Simulate 50 concurrent users successfully submitting valid speaker registration forms.
expected_outcome: All 50 valid submissions are successfully processed, and all associated data is accurately stored without loss or corruption.

title: Single speaker registration form submission reliability
scenario_description: A single user submits a valid speaker registration form under normal system load.
expected_outcome: The form data is successfully processed, and all information is accurately stored without issues.

title: Clear visual confirmation after successful registration
scenario_description: A user successfully completes and submits the speaker registration form.
expected_outcome: The user is immediately redirected to a dedicated "Thank You" or confirmation page, clearly indicating successful submission.

title: Immediate persistent success message after registration
scenario_description: A user successfully completes and submits the speaker registration form, where an inline message is expected.
expected_outcome: A clear, prominent, and persistent success message appears on the page, confirming successful submission without requiring a page refresh.
